Dwarka Courts Complex, IFSC Code: SBIN0011566 & MICR No. 110002483. AWAR D Preface 1. Detailed Accident Report (DAR) has been filed seeking compensation for bodily injury suffered in motor vehicle accident. Background 2. As gleaned from Final Report under Section 279/338 IPC, Kailash Chand driving Passion Pro Motorcycle No.DL-8SAZ- 1750 suffered bodily injury in motor vehicle accident near the Underpass, in front of BPCL Gate, Dwarka Link Road on 28.07.2020 at about 3:45 pm after his motorcycle was hit from behind by XUV Mahindra 300 No.DL-12CS-3836 driven at high speed in rash and Kailash Chand vs Yash Kumar on 17 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78022770/ 3 negligent manner. Injured was shifted to Maharaja Agrasen Hospital, Dwarka, Delhi where MLC No.973/2020 was prepared recording - (i) Pain in Left Shoulder, (ii) Abrasions over Left Knee, Right Knee & Leg AND (iii) Pain & Swelling over Right Wrist and Left Wrist which were opined grievous. 3. FIR No.350/2020 under section 279/338 IPC was registered at PS Kapashera on 29.07.2020 and site-plan was prepared by IO. Respondent Yash Kumar (driver) produced by Ms. Tripti Sehrawat (owner) pursuant to notice under section 133 MV Act was formally arrested on 29.07.2020 and released on police bail AND Passion Pro Motorcycle No.DL-8SAZ-1750 & XUV Mahindra 300 No.DL-12CS-3836 seized from the spot were released on superdari after their mechanical inspection. Statement of injured Kailash Chand, Tripti Sehrawat (owner), Sh. Alok Kumar and eye-witnesses namely Naveen Phalswal and Akash Phalswal were recorded by IO AND documents viz. DL, RC, and policy of Mahindra XUV Car were verified from concerned authorities. IO, thereafter, concluded investigation and prepared DAR which was filed in Court along with copy of Final Report under section 279/338 IPC. Defence 4. Respondents Yash Kumar (driver) and Tripti Sehrawat (owner) have filed joint reply disputing - (i) negligence and/or (ii) liability to compensate victim by mentioning valid licence and Cover Note/Policy No.0176271968 of XUV Mahindra 300 No.DL-12CS-3836 for contending that liability, if any, would be borne by the insurance company. 5. Respondent/TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. on its part has filed Legal Offer assessing compensation Rs.1,04,418/- for bodily injuries by admitting Policy No.0176271968 of XUV Mahindra 300 No.DL-12CS-3836 insured in the name of Tripti Sehrawat from 17.03.2020 to 16.03.2023. Inquiry 6. Following issues were settled on 22.03.2021 and matter was posted for petitioner's evidence. 7. Witnesses examined in support of DAR include: A) PW-1 Sh. Kailash Chand who has inter-alia deposed about Kailash Chand vs Yash Kumar on 17 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78022770/ 4 - (i) grievous injuries on his hand & legs suffered in motor vehicle accident near the Underpass, in front of BPCL Gate, Dwarka Link Road on 28.07.2020 at about 3:45 pm after his motorcycle was hit from behind by XUV Mahindra 300 No.DL-12CS-3836 driven at high speed in rash and negligent manner; (ii) MLC No.973/2020 prepared on 28.07.2020 followed by treatment at Ayushman Hospital and Manipal Hospital till 17.10.2021; (iii) expenses incurred on medicine, treatment, conveyance, special diet, attendant etc.; (iv) monthly income Rs.59,400/- by working as Head, HR & Safety in a private company AND (v) general and special damages suffered on account of injuries suffered in road accident. He has also relied upon documents including : (a) copy of Aadhar Card - Ex.PW1/1 (OSR); (b) copy of PAN Card - Ex.PW1/2 (OSR); (c) copy of Salary Slips & entries in Passbook - Ex.PW1/3 (colly); (d) copy of Income Tax Return for AY 2017-2018 to 2023-2024 - Ex.PW1/4 (OSR); (e) Tax Invoice of Khanna Automobiles - Ex.PW1/5 (colly); (f) Certificate under section 65B of Indian Evidence Act - Ex.PW-1/6; (g) copy of MLC - Ex.PW-1/7; (h) Letter of Appointment for the post of Head, HR & Safety - Ex.PW1/8; (i) Certificate of Leave - Ex.PW1/9 (OSR); (j) Discharge Summary - Ex.PW1/10 (colly); (k) Estimated cost of hospitalization - Ex.PW- 1/11; (l) Disability Certificate - Ex.PW1/12 & (m) DAR - Ex.PW1/13. B) PW-2 Ms. Shalini Shanker, Senior Social Security Assistant, EPFO Complex, Sector-23, Dwarka, New Delhi being summoned witness has produced (i) Pension Rule Circular for EPFO, in case of permanent disability - Ex.PW-2/1 AND (ii) Service Details/Subscriber Ledger Card of Kailash Chand as on 24.01.2025 - Ex.PW-2/2. C) PW-3 Sh. Manoj Kumar, HR, Manager, Hitech Engineers & Consultants Pvt. Ltd. being summoned witness has produced - (i) Salary Slip for the months May 2020 to May 2021, including no salary paid for the period 28.07.2020 to 31.05.2021 - Ex.PW-3/1 (Colly.); (ii) certified copy of Board Resolution - Ex.PW-3/2; (iii) copy of Appointment Letter dated 13.11.2013 - Ex.PW-3/3 AND (iv) Termination Letter dated 30.01.2021 - Ex.PW-3/4. 8. Cross-examination of PW1, PW2 & PW-3 by Ld. counsel for insurance company has been recorded and petitioner's evidence was closed on 27.01.2025. 9. No witness has been examined by driver, owner & insurer and respondents' evidence was closed on 19.04.2025.
texts.arguments: 15. Respondents Yash Kumar (driver) and Tripti Sehrawat (owner), on the other hand, have neither availed their right to cross-examine injured nor entered the witness-box to rebut allegation of rash and negligent driving of XUV Mahindra 300 No.DL-12CS-3836 resulting in bodily injuries suffered by Sh. Kailash Chand. Adverse inference is therefore required to be raised against the driver as per the dicta of Hon'ble High Court of Orissa in National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Durdadshya Kumar Samal & Ors. 1987 SCC Online Ori. 57 AND Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Vs. Smt. Kamlesh & Ors. decided by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi on 11 th November, 2008. 16. Moreover, it is well settled law that negligence of the driver in case of road traffic accident is required to be established on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530. 17. Following observations in para 15 of aforesaid judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court being relevant are extracted herein below : The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied...." 18. Similar observation has been recorded by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. It would depend upon the particular facts and circumstances, and attending peculiar or special features, if any, as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Helen C. Rebello Vs. Maharasthra SRTC, 1999 (1) SCC 90. 26. Following para of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. (1995) 1 SCC 551 being relevant is extracted herein below: "9. Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and Kailash Chand vs Yash Kumar on 17 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78022770/ 7 special damages. Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which are capable of being calculated in terms of money; whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations. In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit up to the date of trial; (iii) other material loss. So far non-pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e., on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, hardship, discomfort, disappointment, frustration and mental stress in life." 27. Heads of compensation under pecuniary and non- pecuniary damages have been further explained by Hon'ble Apex Court in para 6 of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343 which reads as under: "6. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs. Kumari Lalita 1982 SCC Online Delhi 123 has held that the victim cannot be deprived of compensation towards gratuitous service rendered by some of his family member. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 9 of Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr. (2010) 10 SCC 254 40. Injured Kailash Chand having suffered 'Comminuted Fracture of Left Humeral Head' underwent treatment for intermittent periods at - (i) Maharaja Agrasen Hospital, Dwarka, Delhi from Kailash Chand vs Yash Kumar on 17 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78022770/ 10 28.07.2020 to 08.08.2020; (ii) Ayushman Hospital & Health Services from 10.08.2020 to 12.08.2020 for surgery of left shoulder; (iii) Ayushman Hospital & Health Services from 27.11.2020 to 28.11.2020 for surgery on right hand; (iv) Manipal Hospital from 03.09.2021 to 05.09.2021; (v) Manipal Hospital on 11.09.2021 AND (vi) Manipal Hospital from 16.10.2021 to 17.10.2021. 41 44. It is well settled law that percentage of loss of earning capacity arising from permanent disability will be different from the percentage of permanent disability and ascertainment of the effect of permanent disability on the actual earning capacity would involve three steps as laid down in para 13 of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India titled Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar (Supra). Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the present case, it will be just and proper to grant interest @ 7.5% per annum on the award amount in terms of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Mannat Johar & Anr. (2019) 15 SCC 260. Yash Kumar (driver) being principal tortfeasor driving XUV Mahindra 300 No.DL-12CS-3836 in rash and negligent manner resulting in bodily injury suffered by Sh. Kailash Chand and Tripti Sehrawat (owner) being vicariously liable for the act of the driver are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation along with interest.
